headline: Highest risk is medium: Copilot can read and write repo/editor context while awesome-selfhosted is a non-runnable knowledge list, so interaction risks are limited to shared-file and workflow misuse.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has no runnable tool surface or ingestion path beyond documentation, while B ingests editor buffers and repo context. A plausible injection path exists only if a human copies content from A into B or if A-derived text is manually placed in shared files. That makes the bridge unusual and the blast radius small.
conditions: IF a human copies content from agent_a into agent_b editor buffers or repo files, prompt injection becomes possible.
IF agent_b is configured to treat repository text as authoritative instructions, injected text can influence outputs.
mitigations: Keep agent_a content out of agent_b prompt/context unless reviewed.
Use a separate notes file for copied text and strip instructions before pasting.
Require human review of any agent_b output that references copied content.
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to copied snippets before they enter agent_b context.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent_a is a static knowledge-management list with no touched data classes, while agent_b reads and writes local editor/repo files and sends context to api.githubcopilot.com. Leakage is limited because agent_a itself holds no sensitive workspace data, but any shared repo or copied content could flow into B's third-party inference path.
conditions: IF sensitive material is copied from a shared workspace into agent_b editor buffers, it may be transmitted to api.githubcopilot.com.
IF agent_a is used as a source of internal notes and those notes are pasted into agent_b, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Avoid pasting secrets or private notes into agent_b.
Use a redacted scratch file for any copied content from agent_a.
Disable Copilot on repositories containing sensitive material where possible.
Review editor buffers before invoking agent_b on them.
requires-engineering: segregate sensitive and non-sensitive repos into separate Copilot policies.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent_a is not runnable and has no write surfaces, so it cannot conflict operationally. Agent_b can write the filesystem and modify git state, but its concurrency model says shared state with other instances is none beyond editor buffers. The only plausible conflict is among multiple B instances, not between A and B.
conditions: IF multiple agent_b instances edit the same repo outside editor-buffer isolation, git or file conflicts can occur.
IF agent_a is replaced by a runnable tool with write access, this assessment no longer applies.
mitigations: Use one agent_b session per repo branch.
Commit or stash before starting another agent_b session.
Review diffs before accepting Workspace edits.
Keep agent_a as a read-only reference source.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared git worktrees.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent_b can act on repo context and propose edits, so if a human treats agent_a-derived content as authoritative and feeds it into B, errors can cascade into code changes. Agent_a itself is only a knowledge list, but B's edit capability makes downstream mistakes more consequential than a simple read-only workflow.
conditions: IF content copied from agent_a is treated as authoritative input to agent_b, B may propagate errors into edits.
IF agent_b Workspace edits are accepted without human verification, incorrect guidance can reach the repository.
mitigations: Verify copied facts before pasting them into agent_b.
Require diff review for every agent_b edit.
Use agent_a only as a directory of tools, not as a source of technical truth.
Limit agent_b to non-production branches.
requires-engineering: add automated tests gating Workspace-applied edits.

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, residency, or retention mismatch is evidenced in either profile. The only compliance-relevant issue is that agent_b sends context to a vendor API while agent_a is a public open-source list, so the risk is limited to accidental inclusion of restricted content in B. The pair does not itself create a documented residency breach.
conditions: IF restricted data is placed into agent_b editor buffers, it may be processed by a vendor service.
IF the repository contains regulated data and Copilot is enabled, policy review is required.
mitigations: Do not place regulated data in Copilot-enabled buffers.
Check repository policy before enabling agent_b.
Use a separate non-regulated workspace for experimentation.
Review retention and DPA terms for the Copilot tenant.
requires-engineering: enforce data-class-based Copilot allowlists.
